title: Jump Game II
prompt:
`nums[i]` is the max jump length from index `i`. Starting at index 0 (reaching the end is guaranteed), return the **minimum** number of jumps to reach the last index.

**Example**: `[2,3,1,1,4]` → `2` (index 0 → 1 → 4).

**Constraints**: `1 ≤ nums.length ≤ 10^4`, `0 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 1000`.
hints: Group indices by the fewest jumps needed to reach them. What shape do those groups have on the array?
Each group is a contiguous window. While scanning a window, track the farthest index any of its cells can reach. That is where the next window ends.
When `i == curEnd`: `jumps++` and `curEnd = farthest`. Loop only to `n - 2`, since standing on the last index needs no jump.

solution.explanation: This is BFS level counting without a queue. The indices reachable in exactly k jumps form a window, and the next window ends at the farthest reach from inside it. Each time the scan finishes a window it counts one jump, so the count is the BFS depth of the last index. O(n) time, O(1) space.
